title: Zero-downtime canary upgrade playbook - Argo + Terraform for private/on-prem deployments
content:
Purpose and scope
This playbook captures a tested, repeatable pattern for performing zero-downtime upgrades of Redwood Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) using GitOps (ArgoCD), Helm charts, and Terraform-managed infra. It emphasizes safe canary rollouts, mandatory image signing verification, and clear rollback/abort criteria. Intended audience: SREs, platform engineers, and solutions engineers running customer on-prem upgrades or rolling Dedicated pools in private VPCs.

Goals
- Deploy new service images/configs with no customer-visible downtime.
- Automate gating using smoke tests and metric-based rollouts (latency/error budgets).
- Ensure supply-chain integrity: all images must be signed and attested before rollout.
- Keep Terraform module changes and infra upgrades decoupled from application rollouts where possible.

High-level flow
1) Build & sign image (CI).
2) Push image and create SBOM + attestation.
3) Update helm values/kustomize in infra repo (automated commit).
4) ArgoCD detects change and performs staged canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
5) Automated smoke tests + metric gates at each stage.
6) On success, complete rollout and promote release metadata; on fail, trigger automatic rollback and alert SRE on-call.

Preconditions and safety checks before starting
- Terraform state is current and backups taken (terraform state pull + local copy).
- No active DB schema migrations with compatibility risk. If migrations are required, see "DB migration guardrail" section.
- Cluster health OK: node pressure < 70%, no pending critical pods, control plane latency in range.
- Image signing key present and current; key rotation not in progress.
- Customer maintenance windows noted if required.

CI pipeline (recommended pattern)
- Build: container build -> tag with semver + short git-sha (e.g., 2.3.1-rc.4-abcdef).
- SBOM: generate SPDX/CycloneDX SBOM and upload to artifact store.
- Sign: cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY image:tag (integration with HSM/KMS strongly recommended). Store signature and attestation in registry or Sigstore.
- Create attestations: include git commit, build env, terraform module versions used to produce image (helps reproducibility).
- Push image to private registry. Image tags for staged rollout: use immutable tags + a separate short-lived tag for canary (e.g., 2.3.1-canary-2025-02-12).
- CI writes a release manifest update to infra repo (helm values or kustomize.yaml) and opens a PR. PR includes: SBOM url, cosign sig digest, expected canary percentages, and rollback playbook link.

GitOps / Argo patterns
- App-of-apps: keep one ArgoCD app per environment (dev/staging/prod) and per customer cluster for private deployments.
- Use automated sync with sync-waves and health checks disabled for critical resources only when doing special maintenance.
- Canary controller: prefer Argo Rollouts for weighted canary (native analysis/metrics), or use progressive syncs with ArgoCD + custom promotion helm charts when Rollouts is not available.
- Argo app manifests should reference an immutable helm chart version and an immutable image tag. Never point to floating tags in production apps.

Canary rollout recipe (example percentages and gating)
- Stage 0 (init): deploy canary N replicas to a small subset of nodes (node affinity/taints) or use ingress weight 5%.
- Wait: allow warmup period (2-5 minutes depending on service startup behavior) for caches and warm connections.
- Stage 1: move to 25% traffic for 10 minutes and run smoke + business-logic tests.
- Stage 2: if no errors and latency stable, promote to 50% for 10 minutes and run extended integrations.
- Stage 3: 100% rollout and final verification run (~30 minutes).

Gating and automated analysis
- Metric gates: error rate (5xx) increase > 0.5 percentage points, p95 latency > +25% from baseline, request drop rate > 1% absolute — treat as failure.
- Use Argo Rollouts analysis templates pointing to Prometheus queries and threshold windows.
- Smoke tests: a CI-run test-suite that validates a 10–20 critical-API flows (auth, basic query, write, read-after-write). Tests must be idempotent and run in a sandbox customer namespace where possible.
- If a gate fails, Argo Rollouts should automatically abort and revert. If using ArgoCD-only flows, have a pre-configured rollback job that re-applies previous commit and marks a rollback result.

Terraform module notes and versioning
- Keep infra module changes in a separate PR from application image updates. Terraform-to-helm dependencies should be explicit via module outputs (e.g., loadbalancer IP, cert ARNs).
- Module interface best practices:
  - inputs: cluster_id, node_pool_count, node_pool_taints, system_namespace_labels, image_policy_config_id
  - outputs: kubeconfig_secret_name, ingress_host, managed_namespace_names
- Lock module major versions with a modules.lock.json and reference explicit module source with tags (git::https://...//modules/xxxx?ref=v1.3.2). Avoid raw branch refs.
- When changing modules that affect node pools or taints, require a manual approval gate: do not combine node pool changes and app rollouts in the same window.

Image signing and admission verification
- Mandatory: admission controller in each cluster must verify cosign signatures for images before scheduling. Use a Sigstore-based admission webhook or Kyverno policy.
- Admission policy must check: signature valid for required key(s), attestation includes expected repo and build metadata, SBOM present (or reference URL in attestation).
- For air-gapped/offline registries: store signature artifacts in an auditable S3-like store accessible to admission controller; use signed digest whitelists updated by infra PRs.
- Key management: prefer KMS/HSM-backed keys. Keep an emergency recovery key available to a small set of operators with strict rotation records.

Rollback and incident playbook
- Automatic abort: If Argo Rollouts/analysis detects a gate breach, auto-abort and fall back to previous replica set. Post-abort, trigger:
  - automated rollback PR (if ArgoCD path used) or let Rollouts revert (if using Rollouts).
  - create a post-mortem stub ticket with details: failing stage, error signatures, failing test cases, time window.
- Manual rollback: SRE on-call determines if immediate rollback necessary, then triggers either the Argo Rollouts 'abort' or reverts the infra repo commit and lets ArgoCD sync.
- Hotfix flow: if issue is specific to image, build fixed image with new patch tag, sign it, and open a quick PR to update helm/kustomize image tags. Fast-tracking requires on-call + engineering lead approval.

DB migrations and long-lived changes
- Avoid destructive DB migrations during canary. Use backward-compatible additive changes. If non-backward migration required, use double-write/double-read adapters and a phased migration plan synced with traffic cutover.
- Migration plan should be tested in staging with identical data volume profiles. Migration operations must be run as a separate controlled job (not in the regular canary) and have their own rollback strategy.

Observability, alerts, and post-release checks
- Baseline capture: record pre-deploy p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates (last 2 hours) to compare during gating.
- Dashboards: per-release dashboard showing canary cohort metrics, request traces (sampled), and business metrics (if available).
- Alerts: notify #private-deployments and on-call via PagerDuty on gate failures, image verification failures, or node pressure spikes.

Key rotation and signature revalidation notes
- Key rotation must be coordinated: rotate signing key only when no active rollouts are in progress. Use a transition window where both old and new keys are accepted by admission controller.
- Re-signing existing images is expensive; instead, maintain a trust list mapping old key IDs to rotation events in a signed metadata document stored in the artifact store.

Runbook quick commands (examples for SRE during rollback)
- Force abort (Argo Rollouts): kubectl argo rollouts abort rollout/myservice -n myns
- Revert infra repo to previous commit: git revert <commit> && git push && let ArgoCD sync
- Check image signature locally: cosign verify --key ksm://projects/.. ../image:tag
- Promote canary manually: kubectl argo rollouts promote rollout/myservice -n myns

Post-deploy checklist
- Confirm Argo shows healthy app at 100% traffic for 30 minutes.
- Validate no increase in 5xx or sustained p95 latency uplift.
- Confirm SBOM and attestation persisted in artifact store and match release metadata.
- Close release ticket and link to release commit and signatures.

Open questions / Next improvements (notes to team)
- Evaluate automatic promotion based on ML-driven anomaly detection rather than fixed thresholds.
- Investigate tighter integration between Terraform module outputs and canary scheduling (auto-tagging nodes for canary cohorts).
- Consider standardized attestation schema across all repos for easier automatic verification.

Appendix: Minimal opinionated infra layout
- infra-repo/ (gitops)
  - prod/appname/helm-values.yaml (immutable chart ref + imageTag)
  - apps/argo-app-of-apps.yaml
  - policies/kyverno-image-signature.yaml
- ci-repo/ (build)
  - pipeline.yaml (build, sbom, cosign-sign, push, create-release-pr)
- modules/
  - modules/k8s-cluster/v1.3.2
  - modules/node-pool/v2.0.1

Contacts and escalation
- Primary: eng-private-deployments on-call (PagerDuty)
- Owners: Ava Martinez (playbook author), Samir Khan (Terraform lead), Liu Wei (Argo/rollouts), Riley Chen (supply-chain)

Revision history
- 2024-11-05: initial draft (Ava Martinez)
- 2025-02-12: added canary percentage recipe and terraform module locking notes (Samir Khan)
